heroHeadline: Day 778: Tepuche Syndic and Brother Kidnapped and Killed; Gunmen Ambush Federal Patrol on Highway 15 as Overnight Shootings Hit Culiacán
heroSubtitle: 778 days of cartel civil war: armed men abducted Tepuche municipal syndic David Guadalupe Ramírez González from his home before dawn on September 4, killing his brother Manuel Enrique when he tried to intervene; Ramírez González's body was found later that day near farmland outside the community, making him the second consecutive Tepuche official killed in 2026. On September 8, gunmen ambushed a Federal Protection Force patrol on Highway Mexico 15 near Jesús María — agents repelled the attack and captured four suspects — before a wave of near-simultaneous shootings, burned vehicles and bullet-struck homes hit at least three Culiacán neighborhoods overnight, with no deaths reported in that wave. The violence follows a bloody September 5 that killed a one-year-old and two adults in Prados del Sur and Las Estancias. A new cumulative tally from Infobae puts Sinaloa's death toll since September 9, 2024 at 3,724, up from Noroeste's 3,353 in June, even as the state's daily homicide average fell year-over-year.
